newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria allows troops, expats to vote directly.
newsitem.headline: Algeria allows troops, expats to vote directly.

text.p: Algeria's Transitional National Council passed an election law on Monday allowing more than 500,000 members of the security forces plus a similar number of Algerians abroad to cast their ballots directly in a constitutional referendum on November 28, Algerian radio said.
The previous law in force since 1989 allowed members of the security forces and Algerian expatriates to give power of attorney to relatives at home to vote on their behalf.
Soldiers and police will be able to vote at their posts or in barracks while expatriates will vote at Algerian embassies and consulates abroad, the radio station reported.

The draft constitution gives Algerians the right to establish political parties but bans Islamist parties. It states the Moslem faith is the religion of the Algerian state and bars politicians from using Islam and the Arabic and Berber languages for political gains.

Two existing legal Islamist parties, Hamas and Nahda, which must change their rules to fit the new constitution, oppose the referendum. They argue it will only worsen divisions in society following nearly five years of civil strife in which more than 50,000 people have been killed.
